issues.description: The problem statement's UML declares the fields numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as type double (problem_statement.md UML), but the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) declares these same fields as int. Additionally, the UML shows getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int while the attributes are typed double in the UML — an internal inconsistency in the specification. This mismatch between the specification and the reference implementation can confuse students about which numeric type to use for student counts and may lead to inconsistent method signatures or unnecessary casts.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the numeric types across artifacts. Preferred fix: update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as int (counts are integral) so it matches the solution and getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int. If fractional values are truly required, update the solution and template Lecture.java to use double for those attributes and adjust getTotalNumberOfStudents() and any related methods to return double (and update method signatures in the UML accordingly). Also ensure the template Lecture.java is updated to match the chosen type so students implement the intended types consistently.
